https://www.baltictimes.com/omniva_to_in.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Omniva to install letterboxes in parcel machines 2026-08-21 BNS/TBT Staff TALLINN - The Estonian state-owned international technology and logistics group Omniva will begin installing letterboxes for standard letters in its parcel machines this September, aiming to make sending mail more convenient and modern, and to provide customers with a unified service point. As part of this change, mail collection points will be relocated to the nearest parcel machine. For larger parcel machines, letters can be posted directly into an integrated letterbox. Separate mailboxes will be installed next to older or smaller machines. "A large portion of people in Estonia regularly use parcel machines located along their daily routes, such as at shopping centers. By bringing mail-posting services to places people already frequent, we are making sending letters simpler and more visible. This gives the traditional postal service a more modern and convenient form," said Martti Kuldma, chairman of the board at Omniva. Mail collection from the new letterboxes at parcel machines will occur six days a week, up from the current three, as the machines are serviced from Monday to Saturday due to high parcel volumes. This means letters may reach their recipients faster. Relocating the letterboxes to parcel machines also helps reduce separate vehicle trips, thereby lowering transportation costs and the environmental impact. Existing letterboxes that are not near a parcel machine will remain in their current locations. Letterboxes with very low usage, consistently receiving fewer than five letters per month, will be gradually removed. The changes will be implemented gradually throughout this autumn. A sticker with information will be placed on the affected letterboxes at least 30 days before the change. The current locations of Omniva service points can always be found at https://www.omniva.ee/asukohad. In 2025, people in Estonia sent 780,000 letters by mail. Of these, 515,000 were sent via letterboxes, a 26 percent decrease compared to 2024. Over the past decade, the volume of letters sent in Estonia has declined by approximately 80 percent. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/17/brit.text: Menü Kereső A magyar CitizenGO a gyerekük bántalmazásával vádolta egy brit szivárványcsalád két tagját, majd törölte a posztot, miután ők Japánból cáfolták ezt Belföld Barnóczki Brigitta Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Ismerős ez a két férfi? Éveken át bántalmazták az örökbefogadott kislányukat, mire rács mögé kerültek. A szivárványcsalád veszélyes hely a gyermek számára. ÍRD ALÁ ma a petíciót” – ezzel a szöveggel népszerűsíti az azonos nemű párok örökbefogadás ellen indított kampányát a CitizenGO Magyarország nevű ultrakonzervatív civil szervezet a Facebookon , a szöveg mellé két férfiról és egy kislányról készült fotót is posztoltak, mint kiderült, a család hozzájárulása nélkül. A fotón ugyanis egy brit szivárványcsalád, két férfi látható a kislányukkal, akik három éve azzal váltak ismertté, hogy a konzervatív irányítású brit kormány oktatási minisztériumának edukációs blogján részletesen elmesélték, azonos nemű párként hogyan fogadták örökbe a gyereküket. Az általában orosz dezinformációt terjesztő CitizenGO Magyarország posztjának megjelenése után a szivárványcsalád egyik tagja azt írta a Facebookon és a LinkedInen is, hogy tömegével kapják az üzeneteket arról, hogy Magyarországon felhasználták a fotójukat egy szivárványcsaládok elleni kampányban. Az éppen Japánban nyaraló család egyik tagja azt írta a posztjában, hogy a CitizenGO posztjának megjelenése óta számtalan üzenetet kaptak, ezért cáfolta, hogy börtönben lennének a lányuk bántalmazása miatt. „Ez egyértelműen nem igaz, soha egyikünk sem állt rendőrségi vizsgálat alatt a lányunkkal kapcsolatban, nem ítéltek el minket, és börtönbe sem kerültünk” – írta az egyik férfi, és hozzátette, nem adtak hozzájárulást ahhoz, hogy egy politikai kampányban, más kontextusban felhasználják a család 2023-ban készült fotóját. A férfi azt is írta a posztjában, hogy jelentették a CitizenGO posztját a Metának, és erre kérik ismerőseiket is, de egyelőre a poszt még mindig elérhető. Kerestük a CitizenGO Magyarországot és a civil szervezet kampánymenedzserét, Teleki Bélát is, hogy megtudjuk, kinek az ötlete volt a szivárványcsaládnak a fotóját kiposztolni a petíciójuk felhívásának mellékleteként, egészen pontosan milyen információ alapján írta le a CitizenGO Magyarország a posztban megfogalmazott állításokat, és miért használták fel a család fotóját a petíciójuk reklámozásához. Rákérdeztünk arra is, hogy kértek-e hozzájárulást a családtól a fotó felhasználásához, és ha igen, milyen választ kaptak rá. Szerettük volna megtudni azt is, hogy mire alapozták pontosan azt az állítást, hogy a két férfi börtönbe került, és mire alapozzák, hogy a két férfi bántalmazta a kislányt, miközben a család ezt tagadja. Válaszokat nem kaptunk, de a CitizenGO Magyarország estére törölte a Facebook-posztot. Cikkünk megjelenése után aztán Teleki Béla kampányigazgató válaszolt is a feltett kérdéseinkre, egyebek mellett azt is közölte, hogy „a poszt nem jogszerű, ezért tiltotta le szinte azonnal a Facebook, és a CitizenGO Magyarország ezért kért nyilvánosan bocsánatot az érintettektől egy újabb posztban”. Facebook-oldalukon valóban közzétettek egy bocsánatkérést , pár perccel a válaszuk megküldése előtt, melyben elismerték, a képen szereplő személyekkel szemben sosem folyt ilyen jellegű büntetőeljárás. A fotó állítólag egy közösségi médiában terjedő posztból származott, a kép és az állítás kapcsolatát azonban nem ellenőrizték le, mielőtt közzétették volna, amit mulasztásnak tartanak. A posztban letiltásról nem írnak, csak arról, hogy a bejegyzést minden felületükről eltávolították. Az érintettektől nyilvánosan és fenntartás nélkül elnézést kérnek, sajnálják a nekik okozott sérelmet, és ha kell, közvetlenül is felveszik velük a kapcsolatot. Azt is írták, hogy a jövőben azonosítható magánszemélyek fényképét csak dokumentált hozzájárulással, bűncselekményre vonatkozó állítást pedig kizárólag ellenőrizhető, hivatalos forrás alapján tesznek közzé. Kerestük a posztban említett szivárványcsaládot is, hogy megtudjuk, indítanak-e jogi eljárást az ügyben, ha válaszolnak a kérdéseinkre, beszámolunk róla. https://www.harwichandmanningtreestandar.text: Drones hit ships in Black Sea sinking one and prompting rescue operations By PA News Agency Share 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Drones struck two ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria, sinking one and prompting emergency rescue operations, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Dignity sank after it was hit by a military strike. Five sailors were rescued, while a search for the other 11 crew members continues, Varna district governor Mario Smrkov said. European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen ‘strongly condemned’ the drone incidents (Pascal Bastien/AP) Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members from the Ukrainian-operated coastal freighter Chelsea 3, sailing under the Maltese flag, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries, Mr Radev said in a video posted to social media. The crew, which included seven Ukrainian citizens and eight Azerbaijan citizens, reported the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones. The strikes on the two ships occurred on Tuesday, 20 miles and 21 miles (32 and 34 kilometres) from the Bulgarian coast. During an emergency meeting of Bulgaria’s Security Council on Tuesday, Mr Radev called the attacks “absolutely unacceptable” and said Bulgaria was seeking Nato and European Union assistance. While authorities do not possess clear evidence on who was responsible for the drone attacks, “logic, as I have already stated, indicates that the result is in favour of the Russian Federation”, Mr Radev told the Russian ambassador in Sofia during a meeting on Tuesday, the government’s press office reported. The ambassador said that she does not have any information from the Russian defence ministry related to the recent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea, but added that she did not rule out the possibility that “these attacks represent a provocation by a third party”. Russia's latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria's territorial waters, which injured Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens, once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea. We urge our partners to step up… — Andrii Sybiha 🇺🇦 (@andrii_sybiha) October 13, 2026 Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha in a post on X on Tuesday blamed Russia for the attacks. “Russia’s latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria’s territorial waters, which injured Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens, once again demonstrates Moscow’s deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea,” Mr Sybiha wrote. He said that Ukraine is urging its partners to step up pressure on Russia, strengthen sanctions and take decisive action to hold it accountable and protect freedom of navigation. “The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security,” Mr Sybiha wrote. “Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage. “This must be met with strength.” The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable. I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea. We… — Ursula von der Leyen (@vonderleyen) October 13, 2026 “Nato will continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea,” Nato secretary general Mark Rutte wrote on X. He added that Nato had already strengthened its posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting its deterrence and defence posture as needed. European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen “strongly condemned” the drone incidents and said the Black Sea “has become another front of escalation” in Russia’s war in Ukraine. “This is unacceptable,” she said in a post on X. “I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. “Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea.” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks to the media in Kyiv (Dan Bashakov/AP) “We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. “Those responsible should be held accountable.” European Council president Antonio Costa said in a social media post that the EU stood in full solidarity with Bulgaria following the attacks. Mr Costa said the growing number of Russian hybrid activities would be discussed at the European Council meeting scheduled for Thursday and Friday in Brussels. The attacks came exactly a week after sea and aerial drones attacked two other commercial vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. A Togo-flagged ship sank, while a Bulgarian ferry evacuated the 18-member crew of a Pulau-flagged vessel. Ukraine’s military did not conduct any operations near the locations of last week’s drone strikes, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who pointed the finger at Russia. A day earlier, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying corn caught fire following a drone attack and later sank in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania. Two people died and 11 crew members were rescued, Romanian authorities said. Russia did not immediately comment on Tuesday’s incident. Mr Radev said he would summon the Russian ambassador to Bulgaria, Eleonora Mitrofanova, for a conversation Tuesday. Share Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... Darko Vojinovic - AP Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save NOVI SAD, Serbia (AP) — A week after a student movement toppled Serbia's strongman Aleksandar Vucic in an election, thousands of students and their supporters on Sunday marked two years since a deadly train station disaster that gave birth to their anti-corruption campaign. The demand for accountability over the Nov. 1, 2024 collapse of a concrete canopy at the station in the northern city of Novi Sad that killed 16 people launched two years of student-led protests that eventually brought about the stunning defeat of Vucic’s right-wing government at last week's parliamentary elections . In steady rain and silence, thousands marched in Novi Sad on Sunday in a gesture of respect for the victims. Unlike a year ago, when huge crowds gathered for the first anniversary of the tragedy, participants this year said they now have hope that those responsible for the disaster will be punished. The students brought 16 wreaths and 16 red hearts — one for each victim — outside the station building. The inscribed names of the victims included children. People cried as they laid down flowers and lit candles. A moment of silence was held. A struggle against corruption was at the center of the student uprising Many in Serbia believe that the concrete canopy crashed because of flawed renovation work caused by corruption and negligence that prevailed in major state infrastructure projects championed by Vucic's government. The station renovation was part of a bigger railway reconstruction project with China and neighboring Hungary . Vucic and his ally, former right-wing Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban together toured the renewed Novi Sad station back in 2022. “It was a murder and a murder demands accountability and justice,” a student said in a speech Sunday, promising that Serbia’s young people will build a more just society in the future. “We will not forget them (victims).” Since the election in which the Students’ List defeated Vucic’s long-ruling Serbian Progressive Party, or SNS, last Sunday, the students have demanded a review of high-profile investigations, including the probe into the canopy collapse. Previously, 13 people had been charged, including a government minister, but no trial was held as the probe stalled. The head of the European Union mission in Serbia, Andreas von Beckerath, wrote on X that the canopy collapse “shook Serbia to its core and moved citizens across the country to demand transparency and accountability.” “May their memory keep inspiring a Serbia built on solidarity, public trust and rule of law," he added. Also Sunday, prosecutors ordered a 48-hour detention of Marko Kricak, Vucic's chief of criminal police. Another senior officer was detained along with Kricak, both on suspicion of abuse of office in connection with a murder investigation. Kricak was accused of orchestrating violence during the student protests , and of personally threatening a female student with rape, allegations that he has denied. After it took office 14 years ago, Vucic's SNS party gradually took control of all state institutions. The students' movement has promised to restore the rule of law and democracy, and root out rampant graft that they say flourished under Vucic. The station tragedy became a symbol of the struggle for rule of law On Nov. 1, 2024, the huge concrete construction at the outer front wall of the Novi Sad station crashed without warning at 11:52 a.m., crushing people underneath as they were waiting for trains on a sunny autumn day. Fourteen people died at the scene, and two died later. A young woman survived with life-changing injuries. Authorities first said that the canopy had not been renovated at all, and promised an investigation. But protests started almost immediately with people blocking traffic every day across the country at the exact time of the collapse and demanding justice. Some of the student-led rallies held in the last two years were among the biggest anti-government protests in Serbia's history. And unlike last year when Vucic was in power, Sunday's anniversary memorial was broadcast by state RTS television, following resignations among officials at the TV station in the post-election week. Commemoration ceremonies were also held in other cities and towns throughout Serbia. An independent investigation by a group of experts into the canopy collapse found the renovation work had been rushed under political orders. The experts' report alleged a “systematic degradation of construction standards” and said that the "state of Serbia violated its citizens' right to life.” Copyright 2026 The Associated Press.
